Petitioners file this writ petition for quashing of the FIR No.153/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station CAW Cell, Nanakpura against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 04.05.2005 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
From this wedlock, two daughters were born on 18.08.2006 and 05.04.2011.
However, due to matrimonial discord, they could not live together and they started living separately from each other since the year 2020.
On the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
She also filed the maintenance petition under Section 125 Cr P C against petitioner No.1.
The petitioner No.1 also filed the divorce case being HMA No.223/2020.

However, during the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 24.03.2021 before Delhi Government Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Parliament Street, New Delhi.

entities.text: Delhi Government Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Parliament Street
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Pursuant to settlement, the couple decided to live together and to maintain cordial relations/ atmosphere for the welfare of the family.
The respondent No.2 now does not wish to pursue her case against the petitioners.

3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no Manoj Rawat And Anr vs State And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198372865/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned ASC for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has joined the matrimonial home with her children and is living with petitioner No.1 happily.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.153/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station CAW Cell, Nanakpura and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
JANUARY 19, 2023/M
